purpose: Teach: 排斥/テロリズム/美化/道義/加担/横領/危害/儒教

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、戦時下の少数民族排斥を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Sakura — you covered wartime persecution of ethnic minorities in your paper, didn't you.
lines.style: Steady, curious opening. Not interrogative — genuinely interested in what the student chose to examine. Warm attention without pressure. A teacher checking in.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、国際テロリズム対策史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I focused on the history of international counterterrorism measures.
lines.style: Direct, serious. Slight pause before the pivot, as if ensuring the teacher understands the intentional reframing. Respectful but clear about her own thinking. No apology in it.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 歴史記述の美化問題を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: You examined the problem of historical narratives being whitewashed, then.
lines.style: Thoughtful, connecting the dots aloud. Gentle phrasing — not accusatory, but reflective. Teacher mode: checking for understanding, not judgment. Slight forward lean.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、近代の道義的判断の哲学を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — specifically the philosophy of moral judgment in the modern era.
lines.style: Calm, steady. Not defensive, just clarifying. She knows what she's doing. Each phrase lands deliberately. Meets the teacher's eyes.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 組織犯罪に加担した内部者の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: So you looked at insiders who became complicit in organized crime.
lines.style: Alert, following closely. Slight tilt of recognition — the teacher sees the throughline now. Engaged but measured. Not accusatory, but definitely paying attention.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、企業横領事件の社会的影響を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I analyzed the social impact of corporate embezzlement cases.
lines.style: Steady, unflinching. She's choosing her words precisely. Not rushing. A teenager being honest about difficult material without performing seriousness. Grounded.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 市民に危害を加えた事案を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And you included an examination of harm done to ordinary citizens, yes.
lines.style: Slow, carefully weighted. The teacher is fully present now, understanding the stakes. Respectful of what Sakura has chosen to study. Not quite a question — more like acknowledgment.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、東アジアの儒教思想史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes — I traced the intellectual history of Confucian thought across East Asia.
lines.style: Final answer, grounded and clear. Not triumphant, but certain. She's said what she needed to say. A small close — breath settles at the end. Matter complete.
